notes: Native oMLX arm (operator decision 2026-10-31): oMLX 6b413c90 (version 0.7.3rc1, MLX/mlx-lm continuous batching) serving the mlx-community 4-bit checkpoint mlx-community/Qwen3.8-27B-4bit@10c35caa (16 GB), served under the model id Qwen3.8-27B-4bit (the run's model-directory link name). It is NOT the hf2q GGUF and NOT the same-GGUF peer. In Q3 it runs only as the separately labeled peer arm 'oMLX 6b413c9 (native Qwen3.8-27B MLX 4-bit)' of a --native-comparison campaign: task makespan only, never the verdict of record. Adapter: scripts/four_agent/native_peer_omlx.py; launch, identity and readiness: native_peer_omlx_ready.py; post-run audit: native_peer_omlx_audit.py.

Launch (serve.argv runs native_peer_omlx_launch.py, which execs in the same process, so SERVER_PID is the server): it verifies OMLX_DIR is a clean detached 6b413c90 checkout with omlx/_version.py 0.7.3rc1, OMLX_PY's venv carries mlx 0.32.4, mlx-lm @0d4d3d04 and mlx-vlm @138d7617 and the editable omlx install of OMLX_DIR, and the snapshot's config.json/chat_template.jinja equal MODEL_CONFIG_SHA256/TEMPLATE_SHA256; then writes {OUT}/omlx/base/model_settings.json and settings.json, links {OUT}/omlx/models/<model id> -> MODEL_DIR, records {OUT}/omlx/launch.json and execs '{OMLX_PY} -I -u -m omlx.cli serve --model-dir {OUT}/omlx/models --base-path {OUT}/omlx/base --host 127.0.0.1 --port {PORT} --headless --no-hf-cache --max-concurrent-requests 4 --paged-ssd-cache-dir {OUT}/omlx/ssd-cache --hot-cache-max-size 16GB --sse-keepalive-mode off --memory-guard aggressive --log-level info' (cli.py:1169-1366). --no-hf-cache keeps HF-cache models out (settings.py:1517-1542); --max-concurrent-requests 4 sets max_num_seqs and the completion batch (settings.py:1971-1973); SSE keepalive chunks are off (server.py:2842-2902).

Settings (generated by native_peer_omlx_ready.model_settings, bound by sha256 in the approval and unchanged at closing): max_context_window 262144 (prompt admission only, server.py:2436-2452), max_tokens 8192, greedy temperature 0 / top_p 1 / top_k 0 / min_p 0, repetition_penalty 1.05, presence 0, force_sampling false, model_type_override llm (text engine), MTP/DFlash/VLM-MTP/SpecPrefill/TurboQuant KV/A8 and ANE prefill/expert offload/fp16 activations all off, pinned and default. Requests carry the same sampling explicitly plus repetition_context_size 64 and thinking on: chat_template_kwargs {enable_thinking: true, preserve_thinking: true}, no reasoning_effort (the template default renders, as in hf2q), thinking_budget 2048 on a fresh user turn and 512 on a tool-result continuation; parallel_tool_calls is not sent (oMLX would drop it; the client refuses a second call).

Prefix cache: hf2q reuses prefix KV across turns, so oMLX's paged prefix cache stays on, in RAM only: settings.json cache.hot_cache_only true with a 16 GB hot tier and a fresh per-run cache directory that receives no SSD I/O (cache/paged_ssd_cache.py:1795-1799, 1948-1949). The re-saved settings.json is checked at readiness and must be unchanged at closing.

Memory: weights 16 GB plus KV 16 full-attention layers: about 64 GiB bf16 if all four slots filled 262144 tokens; KV is paged and grows with real tokens, so the canonical workload uses far less. oMLX enforces the memory guard (tier aggressive) and only raises Metal's wired limit when iogpu.wired_limit_mb is set (process_memory_enforcer.py:175-347); raising it is the root's decision, recorded with the run. /api/status model memory is recorded at readiness and closing.

Identity: q5 readiness is /health status 'healthy' (503 'loading' until the pinned preload ends, server.py:3348-3395). The coordinator then binds launch.json (sha256 in the approval, pid = SERVER_PID, exact argv), the process title omlx-server, /api/status (version 0.7.3rc1, every custom kernel available, one loaded model, zero requests), /v1/models/status (the one served model resolves to MODEL_DIR, engine batched, type llm, config_model_type, max_context_window 262144, max_tokens 8192), the saved settings.json and the startup lines. TEMPLATE_SHA256 is operator-provided (sha256 of the snapshot's chat_template.jinja); readiness records whether it equals hf2q's reviewed template (c3cf9e34...). At closing every turn's rendered prompt is proven by /v1/tokenize (count == usage.prompt_tokens) and the server's session counters must equal the client receipts.
Run as a calibration (no --admission-receipt): different engine and artifact from every hf2q calibration.
